jobs.occupation: Engineering Manager
jobs.description:
The role

We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead our Product Engineering team in Aarhus.

This is a leadership role, not a hands-on coding role. You own the production engine of Product Engineering: the people, the process, and the tools that turn ideas into shipped software. Your job is to build a strong team, keep our way of working lean and effective, and make sure engineers have the environments they need to do great work.

We work AI-augmented. Modern AI tools are a natural part of how we design, write and review software, so more of the typing is handled for us. That makes judgement the valuable work: what to build and whether it holds up as the platform grows. You make sure the team gets the most out of that, while keeping delivery healthy and predictable.

You join the Products leadership group and report to the CTO. The Lead Architect owns the platform, including the production platform. You own the people, process, and tools that build and deliver on it. The two roles work closely and depend on each other.

Your team's work reaches hundreds of thousands of people across the Nordics: job seekers navigating labour market reforms, employment professionals adapting to new digitalisation strategies, and the institutions managing that change.

What you will work on

Candeno serves municipalities, unemployment funds, and educational institutions across Denmark, Norway, Sweden, and Finland. The platform has three sides: candidates navigating the labour market, advisors guiding them through digitalisation and compliance workflows, and companies recruiting talent. One platform, many contexts.

You will lead a team of up to 15 engineers, growing through our H2 2026 upscaling. You will:

People

• 
Take full personnel responsibility for the engineers: performance, development, wellbeing, and day-to-day leadership.

• 
Run regular one-to-ones, give feedback, and set clear development plans for each engineer.

• 
Own hiring for the team, and handle underperformance and offboarding when needed.

• 
Grow the team through the upscaling, and build a culture of ownership and craft.

Process (delivery)

• 
Own the delivery part of the process (build and operate), and align closely with the discovery part (analysis and design), which is owned by the Head of Product Management.

• 
Keep delivery predictable and healthy: sensible planning, clear priorities, and steady flow, without heavy ceremony.

• 
Make sure AI tools are used well across the team, so we work faster and still build the right things.

• 
Remove blockers and protect focus time so the team can deliver.

Tools

• 
Own the development and test environments, and keep them reliable, fast, and fit for purpose.

• 
Work with the Lead Architect so tooling and environments fit the platform and production setup.

• 
Keep improving the developer experience as the team grows.

Who we are looking for

You are an engineering leader who builds strong teams and lean delivery. You have a solid engineering background, enough to earn the respect of senior engineers and to partner with a Lead Architect, even if you are no longer hands-on in code.

You will need:

• 
Proven experience leading and developing software engineering teams, with real people management responsibility.

• 
A track record of building lean, effective delivery in a fast-moving SaaS or product company.

• 
A solid engineering background across modern web or SaaS development.

• 
Experience with modern delivery tooling: development and test environments, CI/CD, containers, and running services in the cloud.

• 
A considered approach to AI. You help a team use modern AI tools well, and keep a critical eye on what they produce.

• 
Experience hiring, and comfort handling performance and difficult conversations.

• 
Clear communication. You can align engineers, product, and leadership, and make it feel simple.

• 
The kind of person who does well here:

• 
A leader people want to work for: supportive, clear, and fair.

• 
Decisive. You own the hard calls on people and priorities.

• 
Bias for a lean, pragmatic process over heavy structure.

• 
Curious about the problem, not only the delivery.

• 
Direct. You give feedback clearly and push back when something is not right.

What the first six months look like

After one month

You know the team, the platform, and our discovery and delivery process. You have started one-to-ones and built trust with each engineer, and you understand the current state of our development and test environments.

After three months

You own the development process day to day, with clear priorities and steady delivery. Each engineer has a development plan, and you have a plan for improving the environments. You are an active member of the Products leadership group.

After six months

Your team delivers predictably and owns its way of working. You have grown the team as planned through the upscaling, with a strong hiring bar, and you have measurably improved delivery, developer experience, and the environments.

Working at Candeno

We are a scale-up. That means real ownership, real impact, and a product that is still being shaped by the people who work on it.

We are based in Aarhus, and this is an on-site role. You join the Products leadership group, reporting to the CTO, and you work closely with the Lead Architect, the Head of Product Management, and the Product Support Manager.

We are direct and focused on doing the right thing for users. We share work early and expect you to do the same.

What we offer

• 
Pension scheme and health insurance

• 
5 extra days off after 2 years of seniority (10 in total)

• 
Daily lunch from Meyers Madhus

• 
A shared milestone programme that celebrates successes big and small

• 
An active social life: team events, clubs, and an engaged social committee

Before you apply

This is a fully on-site role in Aarhus with no remote option. You must already have the right to work in Denmark and be able to be in our office every working day from your start date. We do not offer visa sponsorship or relocation support. Applications that do not meet these conditions will not be considered, so please only apply if all of them apply to you.

The process

• 
A short screening call

• 
A first interview, a deeper conversation about your experience and the role

• 
A case interview, a practical brief sent in advance

No cover letter. You will answer three short questions when you apply.

About Candeno

Candeno is a Nordic employment technology company based in Aarhus. We build the platform that connects candidates, advisors, and companies across municipalities, unemployment funds, and educational institutions in Denmark, Norway, Sweden, and Finland. Our work sits at the intersection of public sector compliance and modern product thinking, and we take both seriously.

jobs.occupation: Senior Specialist, Global Process Monitoring
jobs.description:
_Do you enjoy turning complex process and operational data into meaningful improvements? And would you like to help build a more connected, data-driven way of monitoring and improving global processes?

_As our new Senior Specialist, Global Process Monitoring, you will help make the health of our global Order-to-Cash processes visible, measurable and actionable. You will work across functions and regions to identify systemic issues, uncover their root causes and ensure that sustainable improvements are implemented at the source, rather than repeatedly resolving the same symptoms.

**Your role

**Joining Global Operations Excellence, you will take ownership of global process monitoring, bringing together insights from local process-monitoring teams across our Distribution Centres.

Through regular end-to-end monitoring, you will transform process and ERP data into early warnings, actionable insights and clear improvement priorities. With a global overview of process performance and bottlenecks, you will help ensure that the right issues receive the right attention from Distribution Centres, Global Process Owners and other key stakeholders.

You will work closely with colleagues across Operations, Application Management, Master Data, Global Business Services, Data & Analytics, Digital & Technology and Finance. You will also help identify opportunities where analytics, data and AI-enabled capabilities can improve operational performance and create measurable business value.

**Key Responsibilities

**

• Own the global process-monitoring approach, incorporating insights from local teams across our Distribution Centres.

• Proactively identify issues and improvement opportunities throughout the end-to-end Order-to-Cash process.

• Turn process and ERP data into early warnings, root-cause insights and actionable recommendations.

• Govern and prioritise the global issue-resolution backlog together with Global Process Owners and Distribution Centres.

• Drive alignment across regions, Distribution Centres and global functions to support continuous process improvement.

• Identify opportunities for AI-enabled process optimisation.

• Build strong partnerships across Operations, Data & Analytics, and Digital & Technology.

• Support the adoption of increasingly data-driven and AI-enabled ways of working across Operation.

**What You Bring

**You combine a strong analytical mindset with the ability to influence, collaborate and create progress across functions. You are comfortable navigating complex processes and can translate data and operational insights into clear priorities and sustainable improvements.

**We Imagine That You Have

**

• Approximately three to five years of relevant experience, or an equivalent combination of education and professional experience.

• Experience within analytics, performance management, process improvement or operational excellence.

• A strong understanding of KPI frameworks, business-performance measurement and data-driven decision-making.

• Experience working across multiple operational functions, ideally within an international or global environment.

• The ability to influence stakeholders and establish alignment across teams and functions.

• An understanding of modern analytics, data governance and AI-enabled business capabilities.

• A bachelor’s degree within Supply Chain Management, Operations Management, Business Administration, Engineering, Economics, Analytics, Data Management or a related discipline.

• Experience working with reporting and analytics platforms, together with strong Microsoft Office skills.

• Professional fluency in written and spoken English.

**Your personal qualities

**You are curious, proactive and motivated by solving problems at their source. You approach challenges with a strategic and analytical mindset, while remaining collaborative and approachable in your work with others.

You communicate complex topics clearly, make considered decisions and maintain momentum across different stakeholder groups. Most importantly, you bring a continuous-improvement mindset and a genuine interest in how data, technology and AI can contribute to better business processes

**Additional Information

**

• Global Career Band 5A

**Did we get your attention?

**If you see yourself in the position and would like to become a part of Pandora’s future, please do not hesitate to apply. We look forward to hearing from you!

We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible.

You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site www.pandoragroup.com.

**About Pandora

**Pandora is the world's largest jewellery brand, specialising in the design, crafting and marketing of accessible luxury jewellery made from high-quality materials. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, Pandora employs around 39,000 people worldwide and crafts its jewellery with 100% recycled silver and gold. Pandora is committed to leadership in sustainability and has set out to halve greenhouse gas emissions across its value chain by 2030. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion (EUR 4.4 billion) in 2025.

Recognised by the Financial Times as one of Europe’s Best Workplaces and ranked #1 among Danish companies, Pandora is committed to building an inclusive and diverse workplace. We believe that reflecting the diversity of society in how we engage with our customers is essential to fulfilling our purpose: to give a voice to people’s loves. We are dedicated to nurturing a culture where everyone feels respected, valued, and empowered to thrive.

jobs.occupation: People Partner
jobs.description:
Make an impact with us

At Milestone Systems, what you do matters. People are at the heart of everything we do, grounded in integrity, collaboration, strong relationships, and a curiosity that drives continuous learning. It is how we work together, learn from one another, embrace new perspectives, and create lasting impact.

In this role, you will be a trusted partner to managers and teams, helping them turn business priorities into value adding people actions. You will create impact through thoughtful coaching, strong relationships and the confidence to help managers build strong teams.

About the role

As People Partner, you will own the people partnership for your assigned business areas. You will work closely with managers, leadership teams and, when relevant, their teams to strengthen leadership, engagement, performance and organisational effectiveness.

You will report to the Head of People & Culture HQ and become part of our global People & Culture team, collaborating with colleagues across regions and specialist areas.

What makes this role interesting is the breadth. One day you may coach a manager through a sensitive performance conversation; the next, you may facilitate a leadership-team workshop, support a recruitment process or turn engagement insights into focused action. You will have room to influence, while staying close to the managers and teams you support.

What you will do

• Partner with managers, leadership teams and, when relevant, their teams to understand business priorities and translate them into focused people plans and actions.

• Coach and challenge managers on leadership dilemmas, team effectiveness, engagement, development and retention, building their confidence to lead well.

• Guide managers through employee relations and performance matters including difficult conversations, performance improvement plans, disciplinary issues and terminations, with clear documentation and sound judgement.

• Drive key people processes such as talent reviews, performance management, annual salary review and individual development follow-up.

• Use people data and insight including engagement results and workforce information, to identify priorities, support decisions and follow through on actions.

• Support organisation design, workforce planning and change by facilitating discussions, challenging assumptions and helping leaders make sustainable decisions.

• Support recruitment and facilitate team interventions by partnering with hiring managers on recruitments, and by planning and facilitating workshops for leadership teams and employee groups.

What you bring

We are looking for someone with:

• 5-8 years of experience as an HR Business Partner, People Partner or in a comparable broad people role, ideally in an international or matrix organisation.

• Strong experience coaching and advising managers at different levels, with the credibility to be supportive, candid and appropriately challenging.

• Hands-on experience with performance management and employee relations, including sensitive conversations, performance improvement and organisational change.

• A good understanding of talent, engagement, workforce planning, organisation design and reward processes, and how these areas connect to business outcomes.

• The ability to use people data to spot patterns, frame choices and support practical decision-making.

• Strong facilitation, communication and stakeholder-management skills, with fluency in English.

• A relevant degree or equivalent practical experience in HR, People & Culture, business or organisational development.

How you will make a difference

• You will thrive in this role if you are curious about the business, easy to work with and motivated by helping managers succeed rather than taking ownership away from them.

• You build trust quickly, keep momentum when topics are complex and can move comfortably between strategic perspective and hands-on support.

• You are decisive and comfortable working independently, while knowing that support and sparring from colleagues are always close at hand.

• You bring empathy to sensitive situations, but you are also clear, pragmatic and willing to challenge when it matters.

Meet the team

You’ll join People & Culture HQ, a collaborative team of 6, working closely with managers, employees and specialist colleagues across Milestone. We care about making People & Culture support useful, consistent and close to the business.

We share perspectives, help each other and keep things practical. You will have space to shape your partnerships and contribute to how our People Partner model continues to develop.

How we support you

At Milestone, we want you to have the opportunity to do meaningful work, develop your skills and grow your career.

We offer you:

• Individual development plans aligned with your career goals

• Access to training, learning resources, and certifications

• Flexible working arrangements

• Supportive leadership and regular feedback

• Opportunities for cross-functional and cross-regional collaboration

• Social activities and spaces to connect with colleagues

Ready to make an impact?

If you are excited about working closely with managers and teams, shaping meaningful people solutions and helping leaders navigate both opportunities and difficult moments, we would love to hear from you.

Questions about the role? Feel free to contact Head of People & Culture HQ, Britt Jørgensen, at brj@milestone.dk.

Apply today by submitting your CV in English.

jobs.occupation: Scientist
jobs.description:
**Scientist for Laboratory-Scale Preparative HPLC Impurity Isolation

****Join Xellia Pharmaceuticals and help develop life-saving antibiotics.

**We are looking for a Scientist or Senior Scientist to join ourAnalytical Development Laboratory in Copenhagen. In this role, you will lead the isolation, purification, and characterization of impurities from antibiotic production processes, supporting the development and registration of existing and new pharmaceutical products.

You will become part of an international Analytical Development team of 11 skilled colleagues based in Copenhagen and Oslo. The department develops and validates analytical methods and applies techniques such as HPLC/UHPLC, LC-MS/MS, 2D-LC-MS, GC-FID, TGA/DSC, and Preparative HPLC.

**Your Responsibilities

**

• Isolate, purify, and characterize fermentation- and degradation-related impurities from APIs and finished products

• Develop and optimize laboratory-scale purification processes using Preparative HPLC

• Investigate impurity formation mechanisms and support problem-solving activities

• Analyze, evaluate, and document results in accordance with GLP/GMP requirements

• Certify impurity Reference Standards according to pharmacopeial guidelines

• Collaborate closely with R&D, Production, QC, Quality, and Regulatory Affairs

• Support inspections, product registrations, and technical investigations

**Your profile

**

• M.Sc. or Ph.D. in Organic Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related field

• Hands-on experience withPreparative HPLC is essential; peptide purification experience is an advantage

• Strong understanding of organic chemistry, molecular interactions, and reaction mechanisms

• Experience with NMR, LC-MS/MS, and structure elucidation is an advantage

• Knowledge of GMP/GLP, method validation, and pharmacopeial requirements is beneficial

• Able to work independently while thriving in a collaborative, cross-functional environment

**What We Offer

**

• A meaningful role contributing to the development of life-saving antibiotics

• An international and collaborative work environment

• Opportunities for professional and personal development

• Collaboration with highly skilled scientists across multiple locations

• Competitive salary, bonus scheme, pension, and health insurance

**Interested?

**Please submit your application in english no later than 31st October.

For more information, please contact:

**Jacob Krall,

**Manager Analytical Development

jacob.krall@xellia.com or +45 4193 3771.

Xellia Pharmaceuticals is the global leader in fermentation-based, non-beta-lactam anti-infectives, supplying Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) and Finished Dosage Forms (FDFs) to over 500 pharmaceutical companies across 80 countries.

Recognized by the World Health Organization and the European Union for our critical medicines, we play a vital role in combating severe infections and antimicrobial resistance. Headquartered in Denmark, we operate manufacturing sites in Copenhagen, Denmark; Budapest, Hungary; and Taizhou, China, with R&D and commercial operations in seven additional locations globally. As the only European manufacturer of several key anti-infectives and with a heritage spanning over 120 years, we are driven by purpose and progress.

With more than 1100 employees, our impact starts from within. We offer a workplace where ideas, curiosity, and initiative thrive, and where your role evolves with your ambition. Instead of rigid structures, we provide real responsibility, freedom to explore, and support to grow. Together, we shape not only the future of our company and the development of our people, but also the health of communities worldwide.

Understanding supramolecular protein structures in multiphase food
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Food Science programme. The position is available from 15 January 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
Understanding supramolecular protein structures in multiphase food

Research area and project description
To move the green transition of the food sector forward, there is a need for novel ingredients from sustainable sources that provide the required functionality in food. Designing formulations with plant-based ingredients therefore requires an in-depth understanding not only of their structure and function in isolation but also of their interactions with other ingredients and their dynamics during processing.

This project will focus on protein structure–function relationships using complex model systems, such as emulsions, foams, and gels, applying advanced colloid science and soft matter techniques to embrace the complexity of food. The studies will be conducted at various length to move the green transition of the food sector forward; there is a need for novel ingredients from sustainable sources that provide the required functionality in food. Designing formulations with plant-based ingredients therefore requires an in-depth understanding not only of their structure and function in isolation but also of their interactions with other ingredients and their dynamics during processing.

This project will focus on protein structure–function relationships using complex model systems, such as emulsions, foams, and gels, applying advanced colloid science and soft matter techniques to embrace the complexity of food. The studies will be conducted at various length scales, from molecular to supramolecular and bulk, using methods such as scattering, microscopy, and rheology scales, from molecular to supramolecular and bulk, using methods such as scattering, microscopy, and rheology.

Applicants to the PhD position must have a relevant master’s degree. Laboratory experience with advanced techniques would be considered a plus.

jobs.occupation: Advances in NMR techniques for next generation Foodomics
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Food Science programme. The position is available from 01 February 2026 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
Advances in NMR techniques for next generation Foodomics

Research area and project description
The Department of Food Science at Aarhus University is inviting applications for a Ph.D. student position focused on the development and applications of NMR spectroscopy in the characterization of foods - Foodomics.

Foodomics is a scientific approach that studies food, nutrition and their effects on health using omics technologies. NMR spectroscopy has played a key role in establishing Foodomics and has offered distinctive insights into foods’ health-promoting potential as well as their functional characteristics. However, ¹H NMR spectroscopy, which is the current workhorse of NMR-based Foodomics, has some analytical limitations. Thus, spectral overlap renders substantial parts of the food metabolome unidentified.

This PhD project aims at developing and examining new and alternative NMR-based approaches within Foodomics. This includes elucidating the potential of ¹³C NMR spectroscopy, which so far has been limited applied in Foodomics. For this purpose, sensitivity-enhancement strategies will be explored, including a dissolution dynamic nuclear polarization technique (d-DNP). This will be done in collaboration with a prominent European d-DNP group.

The PhD project will entail studies on new foods of alternative sources and/or derived from innovative biotechnological processing techniques and solutions.

Tasks and responsibilities include:

• 
Conduct research on development and applications of NMR spectroscopy in food science.

• 
Collaborate with a multidisciplinary team including a 4-6-months stay in an international research environment abroad.

• 
Design and implement experiments, collect and analyse data, and interpret results.

• 
Present findings at conferences and publish research in reputable peer-reviewed journals.

• 
Participate in outreach activities to disseminate research outcomes to stakeholders and contribute to teaching in the department

Qualifications and specific competences
Applicants must have a relevant master’s degree (120 ECTS) in chemistry, biotechnology, food technology, or in a related field.

The preferred candidate has substantial hands-on experience in NMR spectroscopy. Relevant expertise in food science, foodomics, multivariate data analysis and good analytical skills is an advantage.

The successful candidate should be motivated to combine laboratory work and experiments, data processing and analysis and ability to work independently and as part of a team in an international research environment.

jobs.occupation: Professor of Shared Decision-making and Professional Development (combined position)
jobs.description:
Professor of Shared Decision-making and Professional Development 

A combined position as Professor (50%) and as Research Director (50%) is vacant at the Department of Regional Health Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark (SDU) and at the Centre for Shared Decision Making, Lillebaelt Hospital, Vejle, respectively.

The position is offered for five years, with the possibility of extension.

The academic position
The professor will advance research into shared decision-making (SDM) and the involvement of patients and their relatives, as well as the professional development required to integrate these approaches into clinical practice. The professor will be part of the management team at the joint centre at Lillebælt Hospital and will foster coherence between research, education and implementation. The professor will be appointed at the Department of Regional Health Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, SDU. The academic field combines SDM with professional development for healthcare professionals. Interdisciplinary research and collaboration across clinical settings are expected and central to the position.

Research leadership and responsibilities
At Lillebaelt Hospital, the professor/appointee will serve as Research Director. Together with the Centre Director, the Research Director forms the joint center leadership. The Research Director has line management responsibility for academic staff and overall scientific and strategic responsibility for research activities associated with the Center for Shared Decision Making (CFFB) and the Center for Involvement of Relatives (CEPI). The two leadership roles work closely together on the development of the centers.

The professor is expected responsible for:

• 
Strategic Research Leadership and Centre Management
The position as professor includes overall scientific and strategic responsibility for the research units affiliated with both CFFB and CEPI as well as their interdisciplinary research group. This includes line management and academic leadership of researchers, ensuring the stable operation of the centers, and maintaining strategic oversight of the centers’ grant portfolio and funding pipeline.

• 
Fundraising and External Research Funding
The professor is expected to secure substantial external research funding from national and international funding bodies to ensure the long-term sustainability and development of the centers’ research activities.

• 
Practice-Oriented Empirical Research
The professor is expected to develop and lead empirical research SDM projects with a particular focus on the perspectives of patients, relatives, and healthcare professionals within different diseases, specialties and healthcare settings, while contributing to the advancement of qualitative and applied research methodologies such as action research.

• 
Development of Educational Resources, Curriculum Design, and Educational Transformation
The position requires designing and developing practical educational tools and implementation resources — e.g., learning materials — that support healthcare professionals’ learning and continuing professional development in clinical practice performing SDM.

• 
Teaching, lecturing, supervising and disseminating knowledge
The professor should teach and mentor postdocs, PhD students, and undergraduate students. Participation in assessment work is part of the position. Additionally, profiling this research area in the public eye will be an important task.

Research activity, network and collaboration
The candidate is expected to demonstrate prior experience with research activities in terms of networks and collaborations. The professor is expected to increase research activity at the research unit and to expand collaboration with other researchers at hospitals in the Region of Southern Denmark, at SDU, the rest of Denmark and internationally.

The position as Research Director at the Centre for Shared Decision Making (CFFB)
The Professorship in Shared Decision-making and Professional Development at the Center for Shared Decision Making, Vejle, Denmark, is established to support the continued implementation of Lillebaelt Hospital’s research strategy and the hospital’s overarching commitment to placing the patient at the center of care.

Over the past decade, the Center has conducted research on evidence-based approaches to SDM and has demonstrated that SDM is associated with high patient satisfaction and improved adherence to agreed treatment plans. The professorship will build on this strong research foundation by advancing knowledge on the implementation of SDM and the continuing professional development of healthcare professionals. International research consistently shows that achieving sustained and authentic SDM practice in everyday clinical care remains a significant implementation challenge. Changing professional practices and departmental cultures requires more than time-limited projects or implementation initiatives. Sustainable integration of SDM depends on ongoing and continuous competence development that supports long-term changes in clinical practice.

This professorship is positioned at the intersection of health sciences research, implementation in clinical practice, and professional development through applied educational research. The core purpose of the position is to strengthen and transform the healthcare system’s capacity for meaningful patient and family involvement through SDM.

The professorship requires strategic research leadership from a scholar with extensive expertise in lifelong learning, learning theory, curriculum theory, and action research, and with the ability to translate this knowledge into continuing professional development for healthcare professionals. The professor is expected to lead the national and international research agenda on how SDM can be integrated meaningfully and sustainably into routine clinical practice, to achieve enduring behavioral change among healthcare professionals.

Qualifications
The required qualifications:

• 
Applicants must hold a PhD or equivalent post-graduate research qualification and demonstrate scientific achievements at a level appropriate for appointment as Professor.

• 
The position calls for expertise in educational science as applied to the professional development of healthcare staff or other types of welfare staff, together with substantial knowledge of and research contributions to SDM.

• 
The applicant should be able to demonstrate experience of teaching and lecturing at university and postgraduate level, as well as experience as principal supervisor on PhD projects and academic assessment work, as evidenced by the teaching portfolio.

• 
Danish language skills are not required at the time of appointment, but must be mastered at proficiency level C1, at the Common European Framework of References for Languages within the first 2 years of employment.

The ideal candidate preferably demonstrates:

• 
The candidate should demonstrate experience with leadership capacity with the ability to lead research teams, drive cultural change, and contribute strategically to the development of the centers.

• 
The candidate holds experience in research management, interdisciplinary collaboration, and attraction of external funding for professional development and/or SDM-oriented activities will be considered an advantage.

• 
The candidate preferably demonstrates experience with practice-oriented empirical research. Research that is aimed at both an international research community, and ideally also at the target group of professionals in Denmark; therefore, publications and outputs are welcome to be in Danish – whether in the form of books, leaflets, journal publications or other material designed to ensure that both professionals undertaking continuing professional development in Denmark and students on undergraduate program are best supported and thereby ensuring impact.

• 
The candidate has prior experience with developing, implementing, and/or evaluating educational programs, frameworks, and curricula for continuing professional development, preferably in terms of SDM-related competencies. Experience of developing and evaluating continuing professional education in clinical settings is valued.

• 
The preferred candidate can motivate and supervise, has proven research management skills, good interpersonal skills in charge of a research group, and has a clear vision for how to further strengthen the research unit at CFFB as strong interpersonal and collaborative skills are essential.

• 
The successful applicant will have documented experience of leading research and researchers, obtain external funding and work across disciplines and organizations.

Employers
CFFB is a national knowledge and competence center based at Lillebaelt Hospital. Since 2014, it has researched SDM and since 2019 developed approaches for implementation in clinical practice. CEPI works to strengthen meaningful involvement of relatives. The centers retain their distinct areas of responsibility while collaborating closely on research and practice. Lillebaelt Hospital provides somatic and mental healthcare across sites in Vejle, Kolding and Middelfart. Patient and family involvement is central to their approach to care.

SDU's Department of Regional Health Research links research and education with hospitals and clinical environments across the Region of Southern Denmark. The Department of Regional Health Research supports research in relation to the person as a whole, the good life and the more common diseases, makes out a platform for scientists and educators and builds a bridge between University of Southern Denmark, The Region of Southern Denmark, the hospitals in the region and the patient. The department focuses on the continuity of patient care across sectors, hospitals, and specialist fields.

Reference 
The professor and research director will refer to the hospital management regarding matters concerning the management of the centres, and to the Head of the Department of Regional Health Research, Mikkel Brabrand, in matters regarding the professorship.

Contact information
Further information concerning the position can be obtained by contacting:

• 
The Research Coordinator at Lillebælt Hospital, Jonna Skov Madsen, Jonna.Skov.Madsen@rsyd.dk, +45 30507825

• 
The Director of the Centre, Karina Olling, Karina.Olling@rsyd.dk, +45 51518696

• 
The Head of the Department of Regional Health Research, SDU, Mikkel Brabrand, mbrabrand@health.sdu.dk, +45 93534980

Salary and terms of employment
The successful applicant for the professor position will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

The position as Professor is salaried in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and on terms corresponding to salary grade 37 of the Danish state salary system. Additional qualification- and function-related allowances may be negotiated.

The work location will be at Center for Shared Decision Making (Center for Fælles Beslutningstagning), Beriderbakken 4, 7100 Vejle, Denmark.

Application
Only applications written in English will be accepted for evaluation.

The application must include (as PDF files) (please note that the application (the motivation letter) and CV must not exceed 10 MB in total):

• 
An application

• 
A detailed CV

• 
Degree certificates (inclusive of Ph.D.-diploma or equivalent)

• 
A complete and numbered list of publications

• 
10 scientific peer-reviewed publications considered by the candidate as most important for this position (please notice that one pdf file must be attached for each publication)

• 
It is permitted to merge the 10 scientific peer-reviewed publications into a single PDF file due to upload constraints.

• 
A teaching portfolio detailing the candidate’s prior teaching experience, teaching skills, and teaching philosophy

• 
Track record in obtaining research funding

• 
National and international research collaboration and collaborations with researchers in other disciplines and sectors

• 
A research plan detailing the candidate’s ideas and plans for her/his future research work

Please note that all the above-mentioned information must be included in the application. Incomplete applications with regards to the above-mentioned requirements will not be assessed.

Applications received after the deadline and/or incomplete applications will not be considered.

The application deadline is 11 November 2026 at 11.59 PM/23.59 (CET/CEST)

Assessment
Shortlisting will be used as part of the initial selection process. 

Assessment of shortlisted applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Shortlisted applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and, if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material. 

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicants will receive part of the evaluation that concerns themselves.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher in Real World Evidence for Knee Osteoarthritis
jobs.description:
Your impact begins here

We are seeking a postdoctoral researcher to help advance PROBE, an Innovative Health Initiative (IHI) public-private partnership focused on patient-relevant osteoarthritis endpoints using big data. You will be anchored in Novo Nordisk’s R&D Real World Evidence (RWE) area, with access to its scientific expertise and support network, and work closely with our Public-Private Partnerships (PPP) team and partners across the consortium.

Your main research focus will be PROBE Work Package 4 (WP4): analysing patient characteristics and identifying factors (such as clinical variables and biomarkers) associated with osteoarthritis progression, meaningful patient subgroups, and potential surrogates of clinically relevant outcomes. You will also help establish the infrastructure and authorised access needed for analysis in the federated database network and contribute to deliverables across other work packages.

What you'll bring

You have a PhD in epidemiology, biostatistics, data science, biomedical informatics, computational biology, public health, or a related field, together with experience analysing complex health data. We expect you to bring:

• 
Strong programming and reproducible analysis skills in R or Python, knowledge of modern machine learning/AI methods, and sound statistical reasoning.

• 
Experience with observational, registry, electronic health record, clinical, or other longitudinal patient-level datasets.

• 
The ability to formulate research questions, assess data fitness, interpret results responsibly, and explain findings to both technical and nontechnical colleagues.

• 
The organisation and initiative to move collaborative research forward across teams and institutions, with fluent written and spoken English.

• 
Experience in osteoarthritis or musculoskeletal research, patient stratification, biomarker research, distributed or federated analytics, and health-data governance would be an advantage.

You do not need experience in every area to apply.

What you'll do

• 
Design and conduct reproducible analyses of patient demographics, clinical characteristics, disease burden, and longitudinal outcomes across relevant osteoarthritis datasets.

• 
Investigate prognostic variables, patterns of disease progression, patient subgroups, treatment effectiveness, and candidate biomarkers or surrogate outcomes in support of relevant research questions.

• 
Work with data owners, WP3 infrastructure partners, internal data specialists, and governance teams to help establish data connections, permissions, harmonised definitions, and practical access to the federated database network.

• 
Apply appropriate statistical and machine-learning methods to heterogeneous real-world data, documenting assumptions, data quality, limitations, and validation results.

• 
Translate findings into scientific reports, presentations, publications, and consortium deliverables, including contributions to other areas where your analyses are relevant.

• 
Coordinate closely with the R&D RWE team and PPP team, and communicate progress and results to multidisciplinary public and private partners.

Who you'll work with

Within R&D RWE, you will work alongside epidemiologists and data scientists who use real-world patient data to inform disease understanding and research decisions. The PPP office will be a close partner in consortium coordination, scientific communication, and delivery of PROBE commitments.

About PROBE

Knee osteoarthritis affects people differently, making it difficult to predict progression and identify who may benefit from specific treatments. PROBE brings together patient data and expertise across academic, healthcare, industry, and patient partners to improve patient stratification, predictive models, endpoints, and clinical trial design. Its federated approach is intended to enable analysis across datasets while respecting applicable governance and privacy requirements.

jobs.occupation: Associate Director, Centre for Functional Assays & Screening Therapeutics Discovery
jobs.description:
Your impact begins here

Lead the people and capabilities that make functional assays possible across our early drug discovery portfolio. As Associate Director in the Centre for Functional Assays & Screening (CFAS), you will lead a department of 12 scientists and technicians, with responsibility for delivering the cell lines that enable high-quality and high-throughput drug candidate screening.

Your impact will extend beyond your own team. You will bring together our Molecular Biology & Cell Line Development community, shape laboratory operations and automation, and work closely with scientific partners to turn research needs into clear priorities. As part of CFAS's shared co-leadership model, you will also help set the direction of the centre and take joint responsibility for its success.

What you’ll bring

You are an experienced research people leader who can combine scientific understanding with clear priorities and thoughtful decision-making. You build trust, listen to different perspectives and are comfortable sharing responsibility with peer leaders.

• Demonstrated people leadership experience, preferably at least two years, including responsibility for team development, priorities and delivery

• A PhD in life sciences or equivalent scientific qualifications and relevant experience

• Scientific expertise relevant to molecular biology, cell line development or cell-based research, with an understanding of functional assay requirements

• A customer-oriented mindset and strong stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to understand scientific needs

• Proven track record of improving research workflows and laboratory operations, with demonstrated experience leading laboratory automation initiatives.

• Ability to set clear direction and expectations while collaborating with peer leaders to make joint decisions and share accountability for CFAS.

What you’ll do

• Lead and develop a team of scientists and technicians, creating an environment built on trust, psychological safety and clear accountability

• Lead the Molecular Biology & Cell Line Development community, developing capabilities and ensuring timely delivery of cell lines that meet functional assay needs

• Build strong partnerships with internal stakeholders, translating scientific needs into priorities and balancing project commitments with team capacity

• Take operational leadership of CFAS laboratory facilities, setting direction for laboratory automation and improving workflows, facility use and efficiency

• Ensure scientific quality and timely delivery of two high-priority CFAS commitments: in vitro immunogenicity assessment of early candidates and transfer of robust cell-based potency assays to CMC

• Share leadership with your two fellow CFAS leaders, jointly setting priorities, developing capabilities and coordinating resources across the centre

Who you’ll work with

You will join CFAS within Drug Function & Screening, part of Therapeutics Discovery. The centre consists of three teams working together to enable functional assay development, screening and characterisation in early drug discovery. You will work side by side with your two fellow CFAS leaders. Through this shared co-leadership model, you will make joint decisions, coordinate resources and build capabilities that support the centre as a whole. It is a collaborative research environment where colleagues work across disciplines and therapeutic areas to help progress novel therapeutics from research ideas towards lead candidate selection.

What you can expect here

You will have the opportunity to combine people leadership, scientific direction and operational responsibility in a role with impact across early drug discovery. You will shape cell line capabilities and laboratory operations while developing a skilled team and building strong partnerships across research.

The environment calls for open collaboration and shared leadership. You will have the scope to improve how the centre works while ensuring that scientific quality and reliable delivery remain at the heart of its contribution.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

jobs.occupation: Senior cLEAN Partner
jobs.description:
Your impact begins here

As Senior cLEAN Partner, you will bring strategy to life on the shop floor at our Bagsværd site. You will turn strategic priorities into concrete cLEAN activities, connect KPIs and performance boards to site goals, and coach leaders and teams to deliver measurable gains in quality, delivery and productivity. Your work helps keep production stable, compliant and ready for future demand, supporting the injectable treatments we make for people living with diabetes and obesity.

What you’ll bring

• Extensive hands-on experience applying cLEAN or Lean, with a proven track record of delivering measurable improvements.

• The ability to translate strategy into concrete cLEAN activities and to connect KPIs, performance boards and daily management to strategic priorities.

• Strong coaching and facilitation skills, with experience guiding leaders and operators towards new ways of working and building ownership across teams.

• Confidence and credibility to work as a trusted partner to senior leaders, up to director level, using data and clear insights to guide decisions.

• A structured, data-driven approach that turns complex topics into clear priorities and actions.

• A hands-on mindset: you are as comfortable discussing strategic direction with leaders as you are working alongside a production team.

• Good written and spoken Danish and English

Useful, but not essential:

• Experience from a regulated or GMP environment. Perspectives from other industries are welcome.

• A relevant Bachelor’s or Master’s degree, preferably within engineering or another technical discipline.

• Experience with Six Sigma or Change Management.

What you’ll do

You will work across process areas, close to production, linking site strategy to everyday work and helping teams turn insight into lasting improvement.

• Translate strategic priorities into concrete cLEAN activities and initiatives, turning them into clear, actionable work for production teams.

• Play a key role in strategy deployment by translating strategic priorities into cLEAN initiatives and actions, and anchoring them through KPIs, performance boards and daily management.

• Coach leaders and employees in structured improvement, daily management and continuous improvement.

• Identify and prioritise improvement opportunities using data, observations and input from production teams.

• Lead cross-functional improvement projects and facilitate workshops, including poka-yoke designs that make the right way the easy way.

• Provide cLEAN® training, build team capability and establish clear measures, standards and follow-up so improvements deliver lasting results.

Who you’ll work with

In Global Manufacturing & Supply, colleagues work across the value chain to bring medicines to the people who need them. You will join the Training and cLEAN team in the Business Support and Inspection department at DPM IO Site Bagsværd, a department of around 150 colleagues manufacturing market and clinical products. The site has around 810 employees.

You will work closely with leaders, operators and skilled workers across the site’s value chain, as well as with colleagues from other functions. Occasional support at another Danish site is possible.

Collaboration, knowledge sharing and a good sense of humour are part of everyday work. We trust each other and take shared responsibility for moving priorities forward.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted to take ownership, make your voice heard and bring fresh perspectives to how we work. You will grow by working across process areas, by connecting strategy with daily management, and by helping shape how cLEAN® training is delivered to leaders and employees. Your contribution will show in measurable results.

jobs.occupation: Internal Business Ethics Auditor
jobs.description:
Group Internal Audit (GIA)

Business Ethics Assurance

Business Assurance & Compliance

Bagsværd, Denmark

Help shape ethical business practices across a global organisation. As part of our Internal Audit team, you will use your audit and compliance expertise to protect patients, support responsible decision-making, and strengthen trust in Novo.

Your new role

As a Business Ethics Auditor in Group Internal Audit, you will help strengthen ethics and compliance across the Novo Group by providing independent assurance and identifying opportunities for improvement. Working across a broad range of business areas, you will evaluate whether key controls and processes are operating effectively while supporting a culture of integrity and accountability.

Your main responsibilities will be:

• Lead end-to-end business ethics and compliance audits, from planning and scoping through fieldwork, reporting, and follow-up actions.

• Assess compliance with anti-bribery and anti-corruption requirements, interactions with healthcare professionals, healthcare organisations and public officials, patient engagement activities, third-party management processes, and data privacy requirements.

• Partner with stakeholders across the organisation to gather evidence, discuss observations, and support the implementation of remediation actions.

• Analyse data and audit evidence to identify control gaps, emerging trends, and potential compliance risks, documenting findings in a clear, balanced, and objective manner.

• Support the development and continuous improvement of digital solutions and monitoring tools used within Internal Audit.

• Contribute to strengthening governance, risk management, and compliance practices across the Novo Group.

Your new department

You will join Group Internal Audit (GIA), based at Novo’s headquarters in Bagsværd, Denmark. As a diverse and international team, we provide independent assurance and advisory services to Senior Management and the Audit Committee across Business Ethics, ESG, Finance, and IT.

In this role, you will collaborate with colleagues and stakeholders across the global organisation, gaining exposure to both headquarters functions and affiliates around the world. Working across a wide range of business areas, you will contribute to strengthening governance, compliance, and risk management while building a broad understanding of the business and its operations.

Your skills and qualifications

To succeed in this role, you combine strong ethics and compliance expertise with a curious, analytical mindset. You are comfortable working independently, building productive relationships across functions and cultures, and translating complex information into clear, evidence-based insights.

To succeed in this role, you:

• Hold a master’s degree or equivalent qualification in Finance, Business Law, Business Administration, Auditing, or a related discipline.

• Bring at least two years of experience in Ethics & Compliance within an international company in the pharmaceutical, healthcare, or consumer goods industry.

• Have strong analytical skills and experience working with data to identify trends, assess risks, and draw evidence-based conclusions.

• Communicate confidently and effectively in English, both verbally and in writing, and are able to engage with stakeholders at all levels of the organisation.

• Take a proactive and independent approach to your work, with the confidence to lead audit assignments and navigate complex compliance topics.

• Are willing and able to travel internationally (approximately 50–70 days per year) to support audits across global affiliates and operations.

The following would be considered an advantage:

• Experience in internal or external audit.

• Knowledge of data privacy requirements and related compliance frameworks.

• Familiarity with AI tools and technologies and their practical application in analytical, monitoring, or audit activities.

• Proficiency in additional languages beyond English.

Working at Novo

Every day we seek the solutions that defeat serious chronic diseases. To do this, we approach our work with determination, constant curiosity and a commitment to finding better ways forward. For over 100 years, this dedication has driven us to build a company focused on lasting change for long-term health. One where diverse thinking, shared purpose and mutual respect come together to create extraordinary results. When you join us, you're not just starting a job – you're becoming part of a story that spans generations.

What we offer

There is, of course, more on offer here than the uniqueness of our culture and the extraordinary results we produce. Being part of a global healthcare company means opportunities to learn and develop are all around us, while our benefits are designed with your career and life stage in mind.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 570,200.00 to 838,100.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

Contact

For further information about the position, please contact Sr Manager Timur Zafesov at TIZE@novonordisk.com. Please be advised Timur will not support queries about your recruitment status.

November 8th, 2026

Applications will be reviewed, and interviews will take place on an ongoing basis. Therefore, do not hesitate to apply if interested at your earliest convenience.

You do not need to attach a cover letter to your application, but please include a few sentences about why you are applying in your resume or CV. To ensure an efficient and fair recruitment process, please refrain from adding a photo to your CV.

At Novo, we're not chasing quick fixes – we're creating lasting change for long-term health. We embrace diverse perspectives, seek out bold ideas, and build partnerships rooted in shared purpose. Together, we're making healthcare more accessible, treating and preventing diseases, and pioneering solutions that create change spanning generations.
